doc.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

chapter: Free playing, time and the Classic Jazz Trio
title: Philadelphia Musical Academy and Dixieland as misdemeanor
summary: He studied at the Philadelphia Musical Academy 1962-66, now an all-jazz school; Rowe shares Don Menza's joke.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: That was ’62 to ’66, the Philadelphia Musical Academy. Now it’s an all-jazz school.
It is. It’s the School of the Arts or something like that and basically it’s all improvisation, whether it’s folk music or whatever, it’s an all-improvisational school now.
I have to share a little — Don Menza said the same thing. He was at Fredonia. SUNY Fredonia. He said playing Dixieland was misdemeanor and playing bebop was a felony.
